record.paper_title: Open problems posed at the tenth International conference on fuzzy set theory and applications (FSTA 2010, Liptovsky Jan, Slovakia)
record.original_question: For n-ary quasi-copulas Q on [0,1]^n, characterize the intermediate class F consisting of those Q whose Q-volume is nonnegative on every n-dimensional Cartesian interval I for which at least one vertex of I lies on the boundary of the unit hypercube [0,1]^n. Also characterize natural distinguished subclasses of F.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n ≥ 2 and consider the unit hypercube [0,1]^n. An n-ary quasi-copula is a function Q : [0,1]^n → [0,1] satisfying:
(i) (Boundary conditions) Q(u_1,...,u_n) = 0 whenever at least one u_i = 0, and Q(1,...,1,u_i,1,...,1) = u_i for every i;
(ii) (Monotonicity) Q is nondecreasing in each variable;
(iii) (1-Lipschitz property) |Q(u) − Q(v)| ≤ Σ_{i=1}^n |u_i − v_i| for all u, v ∈ [0,1]^n.

For an n-dimensional Cartesian interval (box) I = [a_1,b_1] × ... × [a_n,b_n] ⊆ [0,1]^n, the Q-volume of I is
  V_Q(I) = Σ_{c} sgn(c) Q(c),
where the sum runs over the 2^n vertices c = (c_1,...,c_n) of I with c_i ∈ {a_i,b_i}, and sgn(c) = +1 if the number of i with c_i = a_i is even, and −1 otherwise.

Define the class F of "boundary-positive" n-ary quasi-copulas to be the set of all n-ary quasi-copulas Q such that V_Q(I) ≥ 0 for every n-dimensional box I ⊆ [0,1]^n that has at least one vertex on the topological boundary of [0,1]^n.

Problem: Give an intrinsic characterization of the class F. Moreover, identify and characterize natural distinguished subclasses of F (for example, classes obtained by restricting which boundary faces the vertex must lie on, or by additional regularity/structural conditions).
artifact.status_search_result: A 2024 survey on recent quasi-copula problems and a 2024 paper on bivariate measure-inducing quasi-copulas indicate that several FSTA-list problems on quasi-copulas remain active, with partial progress on related questions (such as extreme mass distributions and measure-inducing quasi-copulas). No source explicitly reports a complete characterization of the boundary-positive class F or its natural subclasses, so the status of this specific problem could not be verified.

status_evidence.title: On some recent quasi-copula problems and some new methods
status_evidence.snippet: References 'the Hitchhiker's' problem list of multivariate quasi-copulas and notes a recent result 'may be seen as a solution to the Hitchhiker's problem 2', but does not mention resolution of the boundary-positive class F problem.
status_evidence.claim: Quasi-copula problem lists remain a topic of active research with only some specific items resolved.

status_evidence.title: Bivariate measure-inducing quasi-copulas
status_evidence.snippet: Studies which quasi-copulas induce signed measures and notes that absolutely continuous quasi-copulas need not be copulas; characterizations remain partial.
status_evidence.claim: Characterizations of structural subclasses of quasi-copulas are still being developed.

status_evidence.title: Extreme mass distributions for quasi-copulas
status_evidence.snippet: Studies maximal positive and negative mass over boxes for quasi-copulas, an active line of research related to volume sign behavior.
status_evidence.claim: Volume-sign behavior of quasi-copulas on boxes is an ongoing research direction.
